<a id="galactic-event-advent-war-sun"></a>
## Advent of the War Sun (`galactic-event:advent_war_sun`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 1 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- At the end of setup, all players other than the Embers of Muaat player gain the War Sun unit upgrade technology.
- The Embers of Muaat player purges their faction specific promissory note, unlocks their commander, and places 1 additional War Sun in their home system.




<a id="galactic-event-age-commerce"></a>
## Age of Commerce (`galactic-event:age_commerce`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 1 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- Players do not have to be neighbors to perform transactions with each other.
- Players do not have a maximum number of commodities; when they refresh commodities, they gain a number of commodities equal to their commodity value instead.
- Players can share non-faction technology with other players as part of a transaction. When sharing tech in this way, the receiving player gains that technology from their own deck; the sharing player does not lose the technology.




<a id="galactic-event-age-exploration"></a>
## Age of Exploration (`galactic-event:age_exploration`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- Relics require only 2 matching fragments be purged instead of 3.
- The Naaz-Rokha Alliance&#x27;s ***Fabrication*** faction ability and ***Black Market Forgery*** promissory note do not require purged fragments to match.
- All players can perform the following action:
&gt; - ACTION: Exhaust ***Dark Energy Tap*** and choose a non-home edge system that contains your ships to roll 1 die. On a result of 1-4, draw a random unused red tile; on a result of 5-10, draw a random unused blue tile. Place that tile adjacent to the chosen system so that it is touching at least 2 non-home systems. Place a frontier token in the system if it does not contain any planets.




<a id="galactic-event-age-fighters"></a>
## Age of Fighters (`galactic-event:age_fighters`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 3 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- During setup, all players gain the Fighter II unit upgrade technology; the Naalu Collective player gains Hybrid Crystal Fighter II technology instead.
- All fighters that are counting against fleet pool gain CAPACITY 1 that cannot be used to support fighters.
- Non-fighter ships are purged when they are destroyed




<a id="galactic-event-call-of-the-void"></a>
## Call of the Void (`galactic-event:call_of_the_void`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 1 |

**Effect (corpus):**

After you move 1 or more units into the active system, if that system is in The Fracture, gain 1 command token.
- When you activate a system in The Fracture, apply +1 to the move values of each of your ships.




<a id="galactic-event-civilized-society"></a>
## Civilized Society (`galactic-event:civilized_society`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- During setup, turn all public objectives face up.
- There is no limit on the number of public objectives a player may score during the status phase.
- The game does not immediately end when a player reaches the required number of victory points; instead, it ends at the end of that round&#x27;s status phase, and the player with the most victory points wins. In the case of a tie, the tied players total the influence values of their controlled planets and their unspent trade goods; the player or players with the highest total win the game.




<a id="galactic-event-cosmic-phenomenae"></a>
## Cosmic Phenomenae (`galactic-event:cosmic_phenomenae`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

**Effect (corpus):**

Anomalies have the following additional rules:
&gt; - ***Nebulae:*** Defending ships in nebulae apply an additional +3 to their combat rolls instead of +1.
&gt; - ***Asteroid Fields:*** Fighter I&#x27;s do not participate in space combat in asteroid fields.
&gt; - ***Supernovas:*** Units with PRODUCTION in or adjacent to supernovas have their PRODUCTION values increased by 1.
&gt; - ***Gravity Rifts:*** You may apply an additional +1 to the MOVE value of any of your ships moving out of gravity rifts; if you do, those ships are destroyed on a roll of 5 or lower.
&gt; - ***Entropic Scars:*** Systems that contain entropic scars are adjacent to each other.




<a id="galactic-event-cowabunga"></a>
## Conventions of War Abandoned (`galactic-event:cowabunga`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 3 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- Each hit produced by ***BOMBARDMENT*** rolls destroys 3 units instead of 1.
- ***X-89 BACTERIAL WEAPON*** technology gains the following ACTION: Exhaust to choose 1 planet in a system that contains 1 of your units that has bombardment; purge its planet card and all attachments or legendary planet ability cards associated with it. 
- You are eliminated if all your home system&#x27;s planet cards are purged.




<a id="galactic-event-cultural-exchange"></a>
## Cultural Exchange Program (`galactic-event:cultural_exchange`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- At the end of setup, shuffle the reference cards that correspond to each faction in play. Each player draws 1 of those cards and takes all leaders that correspond to that faction. They belong to that player for the remainder of the game. Then, each player unlocks their commander.
- The Obsidian/Firmament player does not participate in the Cultural Exchange Program. Instead, they begin the game with &quot;The Obsidian&quot; relic.




<a id="galactic-event-dangerous-wilds"></a>
## Dangerous Wilds (`galactic-event:dangerous_wilds`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 1 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- During setup, place neutral infantry on each hazardous planet equal to that planet&#x27;s resource value.
- At the end of each round, for each hazardous planet that is not controlled, replenish any neutral units that were destroyed during the game round.
- When a player gains control of a hazardous planet from the deck, they may research 1 technology; they may ignore a number of pre-requisites equal to that planet&#x27;s resource value.

|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- During the agenda phase, only the speaker can talk; all other players must remain silent except when declaring action cards/abilities. Transactions cannot be performed during this phase.
- When voting, players secretly and simultaneously write their desired outcome and number of votes and pass them to the speaker. After all players have voted, the speaker secretly tallys the results and reveals only the totals to the other players.
- The Argent Flight&#x27;s votes are public and are known before the other players vote.

Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 1 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- At the start of the game, shuffle the alliance cards that correspond to the factions not in play and place them in the common play area; this is the Mercenary deck.
- All players can perform the following action: ACTION: Spend 3 trade goods to gain the top card of the mercenary deck and place it in your play area. Players can use the abilities of the mercenaries in their play area.




<a id="galactic-event-minor-factions"></a>
## Minor Factions (`galactic-event:minor_factions`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- During setup, players are dealt 1 fewer blue tile. Before creating the galaxy, shuffle the reference cards for factions not being played and deal 1 to each player. In speaker order, each player places that faction&#x27;s home system in the second ring, equidistant from players&#x27; home systems (See page xx in the rulebook). Then, that player places 3 neutral infantry on that system&#x27;s planets, split as evenly as possible. These systems are minor faction systems and do not count as home systems.
- When a player controls each planet in a minor faction system, they take that faction&#x27;s alliance card from the deck or from the player that owned it previously.
- Planets in minor faction systems gain all three planet traits (cultural, industrial, hazardous).




<a id="galactic-event-mobilization"></a>
## Rapid Mobilization (`galactic-event:mobilization`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 1 |

**Effect (corpus):**

- After setup, put The Fracture into play. Then, each player simultaneously resolves the following effects in order:
&gt; - Place 1 infantry onto each planet adjacent to your home system (or the creuss gate/sorrow); do not explore those planets. Then, ready each of those planets.
&gt; - Place 1 space dock on any planet you control and place your flagship and 3 fighters in its system.
&gt; - Gain your breakthrough.
&gt; - Research 1 technology; if you are the Nomad player, research 1 additional technology.




<a id="galactic-event-monuments-ages"></a>

Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/galactic_events.json)

| Corpus field | Value |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | 2 |

- When a player gains control of a planet that contains a monument, they may destroy it.

You may destroy all other players&#x27; units in that system and replace that system tile with the Muaat supernova tile. If you do, purge this card and each planet card that corresponds to the replaced system tile.

**Corpus notes (corpus):**

This will purge all non-faction tokens (including mirage and thunders edge) except for frontier and command tokens. Any faction specific tokens (creuss wormholes) will be returned to owner instead of purged. Dane has ruled you cannot use this in the fracture due to the unusual tile shapes.

<a id="rule-breakthroughandsynergy"></a>
## &lt;Tech:SynergyBioticLeft&gt;&lt;Tech:SynergyCyberneticRight&gt; Breakthroughs and Synergy (`rule:breakthroughAndSynergy`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Breakthrough (corpus):**

A breakthrough is a new type of faction-specific component, most commonly gained by interacting with Thunder&#x27;s Edge. A breakthrough will give each faction a unique new ability and grants synergy between two technology colors.
- TIP: Use `/search rules search:expeditions` to learn more about Expeditions

**Synergy (corpus):**

Synergy links two colors of technology. A technology or technology specialty of a color that a player has synergy with can count as the other color instead, for the purposes of researching technology and for scoring technology-related objectives. Even so, a technology can only count as one or the other at any given time, not both.
- EX: &lt;Tech:SynergyPropulsionLeft&gt;&lt;Tech:SynergyWarfareRight&gt;  is an example of a breakthrough that grants Blue-Red synergy.

**Rolling for The Fracture (corpus):**

Each time a breakthrough is gained, there is a possibility that The Fracture will come into play. When a player gains their breakthrough, regardless of the source, if The Fracture is not already in play, they roll one die. If their die roll is equal to 1 or 10, they put The Fracture into play.




<a id="rule-coexist"></a>
## Coexist (`rule:coexist`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Rule text (corpus):**

Some game effects allow a player&#x27;s units to coexist with other units on a planet. When a unit or units coexist with another player&#x27;s units, they do not trigger combat. The player whose units triggered coexistence does not gain control of the planet; if they already controlled it, the player they are now coexisting with gains control of it instead, exhausted. Coexisting structures are always blockaded. If the coexisting player places, produces, or moves additional units onto that planet, those units also coexist. If a player&#x27;s coexisting units become the only units on a planet, that player gains control of the planet.

**Bombardment (corpus):**

Coexisting units can be bombarded. When a player makes a bombardment roll against a planet, they choose which of their units with bombardment are bombarding which other player&#x27;s units, rolling against each player separately.

**Combat (corpus):**

Coexisting units can have combat initiated against them by committing units to the planet that contains them, including units that they were already coexisting with. The activating player may choose not to engage the coexisting units, however, and leave the coexisting units in a state of coexistence. If a player does wish to engage coexisting units, they may optionally engage coexisting players&#x27; units after winning a combat against the planet&#x27;s owner, initiating separate combats against any coexisting player as desired.

Likewise, a coexisting player may choose to end their coexistence by activating the coexisting unit&#x27;s system and committing the coexisting units against the planet they are coexisting on. If they win the ground combat, they cease coexisting and gain control of the planet as normal.

**Control &amp; Objectives (corpus):**

When scoring objectives, a coexisting player counts as controlling the planet they are coexisting on; they do not count as controlling the planet for any other game ability or effect.
 - NOTE: This also means that if you are coexisting on your own home planet, you still get to score objectives

<a id="rule-entropicscar"></a>
## Entropic Scar Anomaly (`rule:entropicScar`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Rule text (corpus):**

An __Entropic Scar__ is a new kind of anomaly. All unit abilities Sustain Damage, Production, Planetary Shield, Space Cannon, Bombardment, Deploy, and Anti-Fighter Barrage) cannot be used by or against units inside of an entropic scar. Text abilities are unaffected. Additionally, wormholes that would be placed inside of an entropic scar are discarded instead.

At the start of the status phase, a player that has ships in an entropic scar can spend a token from their strategy pool to gain one of their faction-specific technologies.




<a id="rule-expeditions"></a>
## Thunder&#x27;s Edge Expedition (`rule:expeditions`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Rule text (corpus):**

Players may venture to Thunder&#x27;s Edge to unlock powerful new abilities and potentially earn the right to claim the planet of Thunder&#x27;s Edge for their faction. Thunder&#x27;s Edge begins the game in play, off the board, with its expedition side - the side divided into six &quot;slices&quot; - faceup.

**__At the end of a player&#x27;s turn__**, they may commit to the expedition. To do so, they choose an unclaimed slice of the expedition and pay the indicated cost, placing one of their control tokens in that slice to indicate that it has been claimed.

Once claimed, that slice cannot be claimed by another player, which means other players must choose a different cost to pay in order to contribute to the expedition. **__The first time a player claims one of the expedition slices, they gain their faction&#x27;s breakthrough__**. A player can claim multiple expedition slices in a game, but must choose a different unclaimed slice each time they do so

**The expedition costs are as follows (corpus):**

&lt;Misc:Resources_5&gt; Spend 5 Resources
&lt;Misc:Influence_5&gt; Spend 5 Influence
&lt;Misc:tg&gt; Spend 3 Trade Goods
&lt;Card:ActionCard&gt; Discard 2 Action Cards
&lt;Card:SecretObjective&gt; Discard 1 Unscored Secret Objective
&lt;Tech:NonUnitTechSkip&gt; Exhaust 1 Technology Specialty Planet

**When all slices are claimed (corpus):**

The Expedition is complete; the player who claimed the final slice flips Thunder&#x27;s Edge to its planet side and places it in a system of their choice that does not contain a planet, a supernova, or a printed wormhole. Then, the player with the most control tokens on the expedition places that many infantry on Thunder&#x27;s Edge. In the case of a tie, the player who claimed the final slice chooses which tied player places infantry on Thunder&#x27;s Edge. Thunder&#x27;s Edge cannot be placed in The Fracture.




<a id="rule-fractureoverview"></a>
## The Fracture Overview (`rule:fractureOverview`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

*The Fracture is an enigmatic area of space that is not connected to the rest of the galaxy. When The Fracture comes into play, the player that brought it into play places it along any edge of the game board, based on player count, as shown in &quot;The Fracture&quot; diagram. They then place **NEUTRAL UNITS** as indicated on the back of The Fracture&#x27;s tiles.




<a id="rule-ingressplacement"></a>
## &lt;misc:ingress&gt; Rules for placing Ingress Tokens (`rule:ingressPlacement`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Rule text (corpus):**

If The Fracture was brought into play by a breakthrough roll:
&gt; - For each synergy color on that player&#x27;s breakthrough, they must place 3 tokens in systems with a matching technology specialty, if able.
&gt; - No more than 6 ingress tokens can be placed in this way.
If The Fracture was brought into play by another ability, or by a breakthrough that does not have synergy (E.g. nekro&#x27;s):
&gt; - For each of the 4 technology specialties, the player must place a token in a system that has a matching specialty, if able.
&gt; - If there are not 4 distinct systems, the remaining tokens are not placed.
Finally, the players place a token in the Thunder&#x27;s Edge system, if it is in play, or the Mecatol Rex system, if the expedition has not been completed.




<a id="rule-neutralunits"></a>
## Neutral Units (`rule:neutralUnits`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Rule text (corpus):**

Neutral units are more dangerous than typical units. They always engage a player in combat if they are in the same space area as the player.

**Assigning Hits (corpus):**

Hits are assigned to neutral units in the following order:
- Sustain Damage is always used first, if able, in the same order as other hits
&gt; Space combat: &lt;unit:fighter&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:destroyer&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:cruiser&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:carrier&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:dreadnought&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:warsun&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:flagship&gt;
&gt; Ground combat: &lt;unit:infantry&gt; &gt; &lt;unit:mech&gt;

**Decisions (corpus):**

Neutral units typically do not make decisions. They will always use any unit ability they have, if able. In the unlikely event that a decision must be made, the speaker will make the decision for the neutral units.

**Abilities and Scoring (corpus):**

There is no &quot;Neutral Player&quot;, however, neutral units do count as &quot;another player&#x27;s&quot; units for the purpose of resolving players&#x27; abilities and game effects.

<a id="rule-otherfracturerules"></a>
## Other Fracture Rules/Notes (`rule:otherFractureRules`)
Source `thunders_edge` · [Engine corpus](../../crates/ti4-content/content/rules.json)

**Relic Icons (corpus):**

When you gain control of a planet with a relic icon for the first time, you draw a relic. This does not happen if you take the planet from another player.
- TIP: If you play Mercenary Contract to return the planet to the planet deck, you can trigger the relic gain effect again.

**Objectives (corpus):**

Regardless of where The Fracture is placed, its systems are not adjacent to other systems in the main galaxy except via ingress tokens. The Fracture is considered to be __on the edge of the game board__. If Mecatol Rex has an ingress, The Fracture&#x27;s egress systems are adjacent to Mecatol Rex for the purpose of Intimidate Council.
- NOTE: Coexisting on Styx does NOT give you the &#x27;A Song Like Marrow&#x27; point.

Sources: [SCPT 336, 1740.62–1768.80s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)

- **Strategy draft:** [X-89 Bacterial Weapon Ω](#technology-x89) synergizes-with [The Mahact Gene-Sorcerers](factions/mahact.md); [mahact context](factions/mahact.md#strategy-connections). The guide values X-89 as access to an answer for ground combat that fleet repositioning cannot solve. Sources: [SCPT 467, 7042.04–7048.86s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/467-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-mahact-gene-sorcerers/); [SCPT 467, 7048.86–7053.60s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/467-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-mahact-gene-sorcerers/); [SCPT 467, 7062.70–7068.30s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/467-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-mahact-gene-sorcerers/); [SCPT 467, 7086.34–7091.78s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/467-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-mahact-gene-sorcerers/)

- **Strategy draft:** [Saturn Engine II](#unit-titans-cruiser2) synergizes-with [X-89 Bacterial Weapon Ω](#technology-x89); [titans context](factions/titans.md#strategy-connections). Cheap mobile cruiser fleets project force, while X-89 is proposed as a way to overcome opponents&#x27; greater ground-unit volume; this is a strategic complement, not a rules dependency. Sources: [SCPT 458, 8231.71–8315.41s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)

The guide&#x27;s default blue route uses both for carrier reach and flexible infantry delivery; adapt to skips and objectives. Sources: [SCPT 257, 4717.04–4799.93s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/257-super-yin-brotherhood-strategy-guide/)

- **Strategy draft:** [Gravity Drive](#technology-gd) synergizes-with [Carrier II](#unit-carrier2); [empyrean context](factions/empyrean.md#strategy-connections). The source&#x27;s round-one double-tech example is conditional on enough resources and a reachable early control objective; with only starting carriers, double-tech may leave too little fleet to capitalize. Sources: [SCPT 476, 7665.68–7713.60s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/476-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-empyrean/); [SCPT 476, 7836.80–7848.02s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/476-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-empyrean/)
